messages.text: A third failure is a request-wide timeout in `declaration_id_and_site_id_agree_across_cli_mcp_and_policy_unit_rows` while its workspace snapshot was initializing. Like the cold-request failure, it may be load-sensitive; I’ll rerun both alone. The tutorial assertion remains a deterministic candidate for an origin comparison.
The broad matrix run has passed 4,844 tests. No additional failures have appeared; the three recorded failures are one tutorial assertion and two request-budget timeouts.
The matrix run has passed 5,515 tests, with the same three failures and no new ones. It is working through semantic suites; the isolated checks will follow after all 14,859 tests complete.
The run has passed 5,816 tests, with no additional failures. It is now in the semantic value-flow suites; the original three remain the only failures.
The matrix run has passed 6,572 tests and continues through symbol resolution. The same three failures are still the only ones reported.
The matrix run has passed 7,015 tests. It is still clean beyond the original three failures and is progressing through symbol-service coverage.
The matrix run has passed 7,778 tests, with no new failures. It is now in usage-analysis suites; roughly half the selected tests remain.
The matrix run has passed 8,622 tests with the same three failures; it has moved into reference-differential support tests. The overall run is around 58% complete.
The matrix run has passed 10,745 tests, including most of the analysis-library suite. The only failures remain the three already identified.
The first matrix selection has passed 11,924 tests. No additional failures have appeared while analysis tests continue; I’ll move to isolated reruns as soon as this gate finishes.
The matrix run has passed 12,441 tests; only about 2,400 remain. The failure set is still unchanged at three.
The matrix run has passed 13,346 tests and is nearing completion. Its only failures remain the same three recorded cases.
The matrix run has passed 13,956 tests; fewer than 1,000 remain. It is still reporting only the original three failures.

A slow analysis test has crossed 300 seconds: `canonical_generic_import_batches_seek_900_oids_before_and_after_statistics`. Nextest marks it `SLOW`, not failed yet. I’ll let the configured timeout decide its result and include an isolated rerun if it fails.

The repository’s nextest profile gives slow tests 60-second warnings and terminates after ten periods. The long generic-import test is still running, so I’ll wait for that configured limit rather than classify it prematurely.

The Linux matrix selection finished: **14,856 passed, 3 failed, 1,855 skipped**. One analysis test took 313 seconds but passed. I’m starting the required isolated reruns now; persistent failures will be checked on a detached `origin/master` worktree.

The cold-request test failed again alone at 4.608 seconds against a 4.5-second budget, so it is persistent. I’m creating the instructed detached `origin/master` worktree to classify it, then I’ll continue isolated reruns for the other two failures.
The origin comparison worktree is at `ebb85aacce` (`origin/master`). Its cold-budget test is compiling its own target artifacts now; once it runs, I’ll compare the isolated result directly.
The origin build is compiling the analysis crate, then flow; its artifacts are isolated from the CI worktree. It has no compile errors so far, though the clean build is taking several minutes.

The cold-budget test fails on both the assigned commit and `origin/master`, so it is **PRE-EXISTING**. The isolated tutorial rerun is queued behind three sibling cargo builds; I’ll continue once a slot opens.

The origin comparison confirms the first failure is already present on `origin/master`. The tutorial rerun has waited about a minute because the shared three-slot cap is full; no changes have been made to the worktree.

The tutorial rerun is still waiting for capacity after about three minutes; the shared cap is occupied by sibling policy, Python, and format commands. I’m keeping it queued and will record the isolated outcome before comparing to origin.

The tutorial failure also reproduces in isolation: the `comment` tutorial query is absent. I’ve started the same single-test command on `origin/master`; it is waiting behind three active sibling builds.

The origin tutorial comparison has waited about two minutes because all three cargo slots remain in use. The failure itself is deterministic and quick once the baseline binary is built; I’m preserving the shared cap while it waits.

The tutorial failure is **NEW**: it fails alone on the assigned commit and passes alone on `origin/master`. I’m now rerunning the snapshot-timeout test alone; if it persists, I’ll compare that one against origin too.

The isolated snapshot test is also queued behind three sibling builds. The tutorial’s origin comparison is complete and confirms **NEW**; the current declaration-identity rerun is the last test needed before its classification.

The declaration-identity rerun has waited several minutes without starting; the same three shared slots are still occupied. Once it gets a slot, it should reuse the already built CI test binary and provide a quick pass/fail result.

The declaration-identity rerun has acquired a slot after a 270-second wait and is compiling the facade test target. I’ll record its isolated result next, then compare on origin only if it still fails.

The isolated declaration-identity test passes, so its earlier timeout was load-sensitive and does not need an origin comparison. The failure set is now one **PRE-EXISTING** cold-budget test and one **NEW** tutorial assertion. I’m moving on to the CI “everything else” nextest selection.

The “everything else” selection has acquired a slot and is compiling its featureless package set, including MCP and RQL dependencies. No errors have appeared; this is a second cold profile build because the workflow runs it without an explicit target.

The “everything else” build is still compiling analysis and the project crates; no failure has appeared. Once compilation finishes, it will run the broader MCP/runtime tests and the selected RQL/policy and cross-language cases.
The “everything else” run has compiled the libraries and is building its selected integration-test targets. It remains free of compile errors; the heavy analysis build is the slowest stage again.

The “everything else” selection has reached test execution: **1,909 tests across its selected binaries**. Initial MCP and watcher tests are passing, including the MCP crate’s separate cold-first-call check.

A new deterministic failure has appeared in the RQL library: the declared-kind-domain test’s observed set omits `assertion`, `binary_expression`, `comment`, `comparison`, `comparison_chain`, and `syntax_error` from its expected set. I’ll rerun it alone after this selection and compare it with origin if it persists.

The “everything else” run has passed 1,866 of 1,909 tests, with one RQL set-equality failure. A Go-named RQL analysis test is marked slow at 120 seconds but is still running; it has not failed or invoked the Go toolchain.

The “everything else” selection finished: **1,908 passed, 1 failed, 874 skipped**. Its slow Go-analysis test passed in 136 seconds without shelling out to Go. I’m rerunning the RQL kind-domain assertion alone, then I’ll compare it with origin if it persists.

The isolated RQL rerun is waiting behind three sibling Python-feature builds. The other selection itself completed cleanly apart from the one kind-domain assertion; I’ll compare that assertion on origin once the rerun confirms it persists.
The isolated RQL rerun has started after a wait and is rebuilding the library dependency graph in the non-target profile. No compile error has appeared yet.
The RQL isolated rerun has been compiling for three minutes, with analysis still the main dependency. It has produced no compile error yet; sibling Python builds continue to fill the remaining slots.

The isolated RQL rerun is still compiling after about four and a half minutes; analysis remains active, with no compile errors. The RQL assertion is deterministic, and an origin comparison will show whether the mismatch is already in the base branch.
The RQL library is now compiling after the analysis dependency completed. Once this isolated test returns, I’ll classify it against origin and then start the Python-enabled policy integration gate.
The RQL kind-domain assertion fails again alone with the same six expected values absent. I’m running that exact single test on `origin/master` to determine whether the mismatch predates this change.
The origin comparison for the RQL failure is still queued behind the same three builds, now for several minutes. The current branch’s isolated failure is confirmed; no origin result is available yet.

The origin RQL comparison is now compiling its analysis dependency; no error has surfaced. The cache is cold for this detached worktree, which is why the one-test comparison takes several minutes to reach execution.
The origin comparison remains in the analysis compile, with no failures. The three-slot queue is congested by concurrent lanes, but the comparison is progressing rather than blocked.

The RQL kind-domain failure is **NEW**: it fails alone on the assigned commit and passes alone on `origin/master`. The comparison work is complete for all persistent failures so far. I’m starting the Python-enabled policy integration selection under uv with Python 3.12.
The Python policy run is compiling PyO3 and the Python-enabled facade under the cached Python 3.12 uv environment. No compile or link errors have appeared; analysis is still building.
The Python-enabled dependency graph is now through analysis, RQL, policy, runtime, and MCP. The compile is still clean, and the test harness should start after the facade test target links.
The Python policy suite has passed 526 of 1,692 tests so far, with no failures. It is progressing through the Go-specific policy fixtures, still entirely within Rust tests.
The Python policy selection has passed 871 of 1,692 tests with no failures. The suite is now in policy rule fixture coverage.

The Python policy run has passed 1,109 tests with no failures. A Ruby receiver fixture is now marked slow at 120 seconds but remains active; I’ll let nextest’s ten-period termination rule determine its outcome.
The Python policy suite has passed 1,572 tests with no failures. Two slow receiver/branch fixtures completed successfully in 141 and 76 seconds; about 120 tests remain.
The Python policy integration gate passed: **1,692 passed, 109 skipped**, including 23 slow tests. I’m starting the semantic-pack distribution tests next, then I’ll run CI’s clippy commands.

Semantic-pack tests are still waiting for a build slot; the three-slot cap is occupied by concurrent CI work. Once they finish, I’ll run the three CI clippy selections and compare any persistent failures against `origin/master`.

The semantic-pack command is queued behind other workspace builds, so it has not started compiling yet. The completed gates remain unchanged: the two persistent test failures are new relative to `origin/master`, the 4.5-second cold-request timeout is pre-existing, and one broad-run timeout passed in isolation.

The slot queue is still active; the semantic-pack run has now waited about five minutes. I’m leaving the concurrency cap intact and will proceed with lint checks as slots free, rather than adding load that could further delay the gate.

Two nextest jobs and one clippy job are occupying the available slots; the semantic-pack command remains queued. I’ll report any remaining checks as blocked only if the shared jobs prevent them from running, with the queue evidence in the logs.
Semantic-pack tests have acquired a slot and are compiling the workspace dependencies. The cap remains respected; I’ll begin the lint selections after this run completes.

The semantic-pack build is still compiling shared crates, especially the analysis crate; it hasn’t reached test execution. Other agents’ test jobs are also compiling through the same capped queue, so this is a capacity delay rather than a gate failure.
Semantic-pack distribution tests passed: 17/17. I’m moving on to CI’s lint-job checks (default analysis clippy and all-features workspace clippy), followed by the Linux x86 matrix clippy check.

Default-feature analysis clippy is running through the workspace dependency graph and has reached `brokk-bifrost-analysis`; no warning or error has appeared so far. The semantic-pack suite and format check both passed.
The default analysis clippy check passed. The all-features workspace clippy check is now checking the complete target set; it has emitted only a non-fatal mbx cache prediction warning so far.

All-features clippy is spending its time in the large analysis crate, with compiler processes active and no diagnostics reported. I’ll let it finish before starting the target-specific matrix lint run.
Both lint-job checks passed: default analysis clippy and workspace all-targets/all-features clippy. I’m starting the Linux x86 target-specific workspace clippy check now.

The Linux x86 clippy check has reached `brokk-bifrost-analysis` after checking its dependencies and language crates. No clippy diagnostics have appeared; I’m waiting for this target-specific pass to complete.

The target-specific clippy run is still in the analysis crate, with both clippy compiler processes actively using CPU. No warnings or errors have surfaced; this remains a long compile rather than a stalled process.
All requested selections and lint gates have completed. The CI worktree is clean; I’m handing back the results with the full logs and the two new test failures identified against `origin/master`.
Handback delivered to the parent session with CI results and failure classifications.

I’ll inspect the new detached worktree and the current tutorial and declaration-kind producers, then update the production vocabulary coverage and regression tests. I’ll validate the exact CI selections on the resulting commit, compare any persistent failures against the refreshed `origin/master`, and commit locally without pushing.

The declaration-kind producer only refines a `DeclarationValue` with normalized kinds that are subtypes of `declaration`; `attach_exact_structural_kind` rejects every other kind before that value can be emitted. The failing test’s expectation of every normalized syntax kind is therefore overbroad. I’ll make the published domain and its test reflect the actual declaration refinements plus the six `CodeUnitType` fallback labels. For tutorials, I’ll make coverage derive from the public kind/role registries and count only executed positive cases, then fill every gap from current docs.

The declaration-kind fix now models the real producers, and the tutorial coverage test discovers roles directly from the public registry instead of a stale hand-maintained list. I’m running the focused RQL regression first, then the tutorial test will report every uncovered kind/role from this master in one pass.
The focused RQL test is rebuilding several language adapters and analysis because this worktree advanced to a new master. The three-slot cap is still respected; no compiler diagnostics have appeared.

The producer-domain regression passes after narrowing the test to declaration refinements. The tutorial coverage run is queued behind concurrent builds; when it starts, it will report the complete missing vocabulary set rather than stopping at the first missing kind.

The producer-side check confirms the domain should include only declaration-refinement kinds and fallback declaration labels; syntax kinds such as comments and regex nodes do not belong there. The focused test passes. I’m now adding executable tutorial cases for the missing public kinds, roles, and Python query steps, then I’ll run the full gate on the committed result.

The Python tutorial now has concrete examples queued for each missing kind, the two new roles, and all 11 Python query steps. I’ve also made the coverage test enforce those steps so future additions cannot silently go undocumented. The focused run is waiting on the shared build slots before it can generate exact expected outputs.
